restatements.text: Details how to calculate the fair market value of taxpayers' assets, including formulas for valuing private businesses based on book value and profits, while exempting certain assets like directly held real property and specific retirement accounts.

Permits eligible taxpayers with mostly illiquid assets to delay paying their tax by opening an Optional Deferral Account, which establishes a contract requiring them to pay the tax upon future distributions or transfers of value.
Requires appraisers to send copies of their certified appraisals to the state and authorizes the state to fine appraisers if they significantly misstate an asset's value.

Assigns 100 percent of the wealth tax to California by default, while allowing taxpayers or the state to propose alternative calculations if the default method does not accurately reflect where the wealth was accumulated or kept.
Allows taxpayers to claim a prorated credit against the California wealth tax for any net wealth taxes they pay to other jurisdictions during the year.

evidence.quote: the fair market value of those interests at the end of any tax year shall be presumed to be the sum of the book value of the business entity according to generally accepted accounting principles as of the end of the tax year plus a present-value multiplier of 7.5 times the annual book profits of the business entity
evidence.why: It increases the complexity of tax compliance by requiring taxpayers to use specific formulas involving book value and multipliers of historical profits to value business entities.

evidence.quote: All interests in any real property held directly by a taxpayer or held via a revocable trust shall not be included in net worth.
evidence.why: It taxes activities unevenly by carving out a complete exemption for real property while taxing other types of assets.

evidence.quote: The taxpayer shall multiply the taxpayer’s accumulated unliquidated tax withholding percentage by the fair market value, as determined under Section 50303, of all material distribution transactions for the tax year. There shall be a tax imposed on the taxpayer in the amount of the resulting product.
evidence.why: It imposes a tax on material distributions for billionaires who use an Optional Deferral Account, increasing taxes on the wealthy.

evidence.quote: All interests in any real property held directly by a taxpayer or held via a revocable trust shall not be included in net worth.
evidence.why: It allows high-income taxpayers to shield portions of their wealth from the tax by investing in real estate, reducing the share of taxes they pay.

evidence.quote: Any appraiser making a certified appraisal for the purposes of this Part shall send a copy of that certified appraisal to the Board, along with information sufficient for identifying the taxpayer for whom the certified appraisal was prepared
evidence.why: It requires private appraisers to share detailed personal financial data and identifying information about clients directly with a government board.

evidence.quote: The Board shall adopt regulations, or publish guidance, further detailing the requirements for certified appraisals and for appraisers qualified to make certified appraisals for purposes of this Chapter.
evidence.why: It expands the regulatory powers of a government board to dictate rules for private appraisers.

evidence.quote:
The following categories of assets shall be exempt from all taxation under this part and also from the reporting requirements of this Section:
(A) Except as described in subparagraph (B), qualified pensions and individual retirement arrangements
evidence.why: It protects retirement security by exempting qualified pensions and individual retirement accounts from the wealth tax.

evidence.quote:
The taxpayer shall report the following at the time when forms are filed pursuant to this Chapter:
(i) The percentage of the business entity owned by the taxpayer,
(ii) The book value of the business entity as of the end of the tax year, determined according to generally accepted accounting principles; and
(iii) The book profits of the business entity in the tax year
evidence.why: It increases the paperwork burden by requiring owners of business entities to report detailed accounting metrics.

evidence.quote: the Board may at its discretion impose a penalty on the appraiser, as if such appraiser were “the taxpayer” for purposes of Section 50312, but no such penalty shall exceed 2 percent of the understatement of tax
evidence.why: It creates new financial liability for appraisal businesses by subjecting them to state penalties for misstated valuations.

evidence.quote: The Board shall adopt regulations, or publish guidance, further detailing the requirements for certified appraisals and for appraisers qualified to make certified appraisals for purposes of this Chapter.
evidence.why: It shifts decision-making authority over appraisal standards to an appointed board.

evidence.quote: The Board shall adopt regulations, or publish guidance, further detailing the requirements for certified appraisals and for appraisers qualified to make certified appraisals for purposes of this Chapter.
evidence.why: It grants an appointed board the authority to dictate the standards and rules for certified appraisals.

evidence.why: It increases appraisers' exposure to state penalties if they substantially misreport asset values.

evidence.why: It expands the state's enforcement powers by allowing it to penalize appraisers for misstating valuations.

evidence.why: It grants a government board the power to develop and enforce new regulations governing certified appraisals.

analysis.answer: Current law was not provided. The clause introduces complex formulas and rules to assess the fair market value of various asset classes for a new wealth tax, and explicitly exempts real property and certain retirement accounts from the valuation.

Taxpayers will face massive compliance costs to hire accountants and appraisers to determine the book value and book profits of their business entities or to obtain certified appraisals for unlisted assets.
Billionaires bear the compliance costs of the valuations. The real estate sector heavily benefits from the direct exemption of real property, making it a highly attractive tax shelter.

Taxpayers are strongly incentivized to shift their wealth out of taxable businesses and stocks and into exempt assets, particularly direct real estate or out-of-state tangible property. They will also likely restructure businesses to minimize 'book profits' to reduce the 7.5x valuation multiplier.

It attempts to solve the administrative difficulty of valuing illiquid and complex private assets for a wealth tax by substituting a standard accounting formula (book value plus 7.5x profits). However, the exemption of real property creates a massive loophole that will likely encourage widespread asset shifting.

Enforcement will be extremely resource-intensive, requiring state tax authorities to audit complex private business accounting metrics, verify out-of-state property presence, and scrutinize subjective asset appraisals.

It addresses the 'liquidity problem' inherent in wealth taxes—where a taxpayer owes tax but lacks cash to pay it without selling control of a business—by allowing eligible taxpayers to open a deferral account and pay the tax only when they distribute cash or transfer value.

Because appraisers face a direct financial penalty from the state if they substantially understate an asset's value, they will likely adopt highly conservative methodologies, resulting in higher appraisals and higher appraisal fees for clients.

The Franchise Tax Board gains significant discretionary power to establish appraisal standards and penalize private appraisers. Private appraisers gain significant influence, as their certified appraisals dictate tax liability.

The effect of a wealth tax on taxpayer behavior is highly disputed. Some economists argue it leads to significant capital flight and asset shifting out of state, while others argue that robust anti-avoidance rules, alternative apportionment provisions, and exit taxes can successfully secure the revenue.
